findings: ERS Lemma 3.39, proof (ghd_02_19.tex:430): 'surfaces of constant x⁰ are Cauchy because x⁰ is a global time function' (and the same for ρ+σ) infers Cauchy level sets from a time function. The inference is not valid in general: on 1+1 Minkowski, T = t − √(1+x²) is a time function (dT timelike) whose level set T = 0, the branch t² − x² = 1, t > 0, is missed by the null line t = x. It holds here because x⁰ (subluminal, cones of g inside those of m) and ρ+σ (on (ℝ², m̂)) are Cauchy time functions. The lemma's statement (GH) is unaffected; it follows from its first sentence. Not formalized (the witness is Minkowski, layer 3); the ETT form is IsCauchyTimeFunction.isCauchySurface (Causal.Geroch), and isCauchyTimeFunction_comp_iff carries a Cauchy time function across Ψ.

findings: Not a defect of ERS or ETT, a constraint on the reading: a time function in ETT's sense (defi:fonction_temps, ETT.tex:1028, a strong morphism to (ℝ, ≤, <)) does not make the causality causal, because it is only non-decreasing along ≤. Witness: the doubled line ℝ × Bool, p ≤_U q iff p = q ∈ U or p.1 ≤ q.1 with both fibres over [p.1, q.1] in U, no chronology; Prod.fst is a time function and (0, false) ≤ (0, true) ≤ (0, false) (exists_isTimeFunction_not_isCausal). So ERS 3.29's 'global time function ⇒ stably causal' (ghd_02_19.tex:354, :360) binds to the ladder node time_function (strict increase along ≤_M), as the binder already says, not to ETT's time function.
